messages.content: I need the Chicago hotel settled now. The stay is Tuesday, October 14 through Saturday morning, four nights. My lodging approval is capped at $240 per night before tax, and I need a straightforward trip to the museum for a 7:00 a.m. installation call Wednesday.
I’ll compare available rooms for October 14–18 against the $240 pre-tax cap. What museum entrance or cross streets should I use for the commute check?
Use the staff entrance near Michigan Avenue and Monroe Street. I would rather walk if it is reasonable that early, but a short direct bus ride is fine.

Three available options fit the nightly cap. The Congress Plaza has a standard room at $209 per night and is about a 12-minute walk south of the staff entrance. Central Loop Hotel has a club room at $198 and is roughly a 15-minute walk west, or about 10 minutes by direct bus. The Hilton Chicago has a standard room at $229 and is around an 18-minute walk south. All three cover the full four-night stay.
What are the totals after tax, and are those refundable rates? I do not want the lowest number if it locks me in.

With the currently displayed taxes and fees, Congress Plaza totals $981.44 and allows cancellation without charge until 6:00 p.m. on October 13. Central Loop totals $938.72, but that rate is nonrefundable. Hilton Chicago totals $1,074.96 and is refundable until 11:59 p.m. on October 12. The employer cap is satisfied by each base room rate, though the Hilton has the highest total.
Drop Central Loop, then. Between the other two, is the Congress route simple enough before 7:00, and does it involve walking under the elevated tracks?

The simplest walking route from Congress Plaza is north on Michigan Avenue to Monroe. It stays on the main avenue, does not pass under the elevated train, and is approximately 0.6 mile. Allow 12 to 15 minutes at that hour. The Hilton route uses the same avenue but starts farther south and would take closer to 20 minutes.
Congress sounds more practical. Check the room details and whether Wi-Fi is included before we choose it.

The refundable $209 option is a standard room with one king bed. Wi-Fi is included, and the room has a desk, in-room safe, and mini-refrigerator. Breakfast and parking are not included. There is no separate resort or destination fee in the quoted $981.44 total.
That room is fine. Is there any construction notice or late-arrival restriction? My flight gets into O’Hare at 9:35 in the morning, so I expect to arrive well before normal check-in.

The hotel lists lobby restoration work on weekdays from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; guestrooms remain open, but daytime lobby noise is possible. The desk operates 24 hours, so there is no late-arrival restriction. Check-in begins at 3:00 p.m. The hotel will store luggage before check-in at no charge, subject to available storage space.

The lobby work is acceptable. Please reserve the refundable king room at Congress Plaza for all four nights. Put the museum’s installation-tool case in the booking note so the desk expects one large piece of stored luggage before check-in.

Before I place it, please confirm the charge: $836.00 room subtotal plus $145.44 in taxes, for $981.44 total. Cancellation is free until 6:00 p.m. local time on October 13; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax. Payment is due at the hotel, with a card required to guarantee the reservation.
Confirmed. Use the card already authorized for this work trip and complete the reservation.

Reserved at Congress Plaza Hotel for Tuesday, October 14 through Saturday, October 18: four nights in a standard room with one king bed. The guaranteed total is $981.44, payable at the hotel, and the refundable cancellation deadline is 6:00 p.m. Chicago time on October 13. I added a note requesting complimentary pre-check-in storage for one large installation-tool case. Check-in starts at 3:00 p.m.; the museum staff entrance is about a 12- to 15-minute walk north on Michigan Avenue.
